test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 23 Sept, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

(O) attitude is

(P) or tendency in individuals

(Q) a broad-based behaviour

(R) which implies

(S) a hypothetical postulate
solution:
The correct answer is** Option (2)** i.e. **OSRQP**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence begins with the subject and main verb "attitude is," which is correctly indicated by **part (O).**** **
 
• Following the subject, "a hypothetical postulate" **(S)** continues the logical sequence, making it clear what attitude is described as.
 
• **The next part,** "which implies" starts the explanation about what the postulate signifies, indicated by (R).
 
• **The explanation continues with** "a broad-based behaviour," indicated by (Q).
 
• **Ending with **"or tendency in individuals" (P) completes the sentence by describing the implications of the behaviour.

Therefore, the correct answer is **OSRQP.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (SQPRO):** This option starts with "a hypothetical postulate or tendency in individuals," which makes the sentence grammatically incorrect and jumbled.
 
• **Option 3 (OPQRS):** This option starts with "attitude is or tendency in individuals," creating a disjointed and nonsensical sentence.
 
• **Option 4 (OPSRQ):** This option starts with "attitude is or tendency in individuals which implies," which leads to a confusing and grammatically incorrect sentence.
